title: Operate and Secure Persistence
readerIntent: Secure, monitor, tune, recover, and qualify persistence.
priorKnowledge: Know the data topology and selected provider.
owner: Deployment operators and selected database provider
summary: Production persistence needs provider-qualified encryption, credentials, capacity, indexing, backup, recovery, failover, and tenant isolation.

sections.heading: Secure
items: Use authenticated encrypted connections and least-privilege credentials.
Keep secrets in governed secret layers and rotate them safely.
Enforce schema read/write and field policy before provider calls.
Prevent cross-tenant connection, model, cache, log, and backup leakage.

sections.heading: Monitor
items: Connection and pool health, saturation, wait time, and reconnects.
Operation latency, throughput, conflicts, timeouts, and errors.
Slow queries, scans, index use, storage growth, and transaction outcomes.
Tenant-safe dimensions, backup freshness, replication lag, and restore evidence.

sections.heading: Recover and qualify
items: Test startup without the provider and mid-operation outage.
Prove reconnect, retry limits, idempotency, transaction rollback, and cleanup.
Exercise backup, point-in-time or supported restore, failover, schema migration, rollback, and version upgrade.
Load-test realistic query shapes and isolation; a local happy-path test is insufficient.
